title: Optimal asymptotic competitiveness for online bin packing
decision_reason: Exact classical formulation, two independent contemporary status sources, full relevant theorem comparisons and separated A27 self-pass; no matching unresolved claim found.

problem_fingerprint.model_or_objects: One-dimensional bin packing, unit bins and sequential rational items.
problem_fingerprint.domain: All finite rational sequences in (0,1], no announced length.
problem_fingerprint.regularity_and_data_class: Arbitrary input sizes and order; no fixed finite size alphabet.
problem_fingerprint.boundary_or_initial_conditions: Initially all bins empty; unlimited bins.
problem_fingerprint.parameter_range: Unbounded sequence length and offline optimum.
problem_fingerprint.quantifiers: Infimum over single deterministic online algorithms of their worst-case asymptotic ratios over all inputs.
problem_fingerprint.normalization: Bin capacity 1 for online and offline algorithms alike.
problem_fingerprint.observable_or_norm: Number of nonempty online bins / minimum offline bin count.
problem_fingerprint.limit_regime_and_order: For each algorithm take N→infinity of sup over OPT≥N, then infimum over algorithms.
problem_fingerprint.computational_model_and_dependencies: No time bound, forecasts, advice, repacking, resource augmentation, stochastic-input restriction or best-of-k selection. No assumption infimum attained.

statement_source_and_scope_match: UB §1 fixes the rational-input model and exact limit definition. HP26 §4 explicitly calls the canonical problem open; GU25 §§1.1–1.3 and EL25 §1 identify the remaining unrestricted asymptotic gap. R_* is notation for the best possible ratio described there, not a newly proposed bound.
proposed_statement_text: Determine inf_A lim_{N→∞} sup_{I:OPT(I)≥N} A(I)/OPT(I) for deterministic irrevocable online packing of arbitrary rational items in (0,1] into unit bins, with no advance input information.
applied_significance: Worst-case excess capacity resources caused by irrevocable allocation under unknown future demand; LB §1 gives storage and cutting-stock origins. Applications are idealized scalar-capacity models.

source_records.title: Parallel Online Algorithms for the Bin Packing Problem
